courses.title: Biology and Society
courses.description: [GE 5B] Fundamental concepts in biology are taught using socially relevant themes. Biological concepts are related to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow, exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigations, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society.

courses.title: Biology and Society Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] A laboratory support course applying lecture concepts through hands-on, inquiry-based, learn-by-doing approaches. Supports students in majors that require fundamental concepts of biology as they relate to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigation, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1110 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 1150 can be concurrent. Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Food Microbiology
courses.description: Cross Listed as: FST 3640 A study of the roles of microorganisms in food spoilage, foodborne illness, and fermentation. Factors that influence microbial growth in food and how the growth can be controlled are discussed.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Food Microbiology
courses.description: Cross Listed as: BIO 3640 A study of the roles of microorganisms in food spoilage, foodborne illness, and fermentation. Factors that influence microbial growth in food and how the growth can be controlled are discussed.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Food Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study of microorganisms in food. Analysis and detection of foodborne microorganisms using cultural and molecular techniques. Scientific thinking and quantitative analysis are emphasized through each laboratory exercise and a term project.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 3640 .

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: [GE 5A] Continuation of the development of fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including kinetics; equilibria, including acid-base chemistry; buffers; titrations; thermodynamics; electrochemistry; colligative properties; and nuclear chemistry. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1220. Qualitative analysis. Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: Introduction to Food Science and Technology
courses.description: An introduction to the scope, principles and practices of food science and technology. Basic aspects of chemistry, microbiology and sensory analysis of food products. Introduction to food packaging, safety and sanitation and basics of food laws and regulations. Principles of food engineering and the most common methods of food preservation. Overview on sustainability and the commercial processing of specific food commodities.

courses.title: Food Laws and Regulations
courses.description: An examination of the rules and regulations of various governmental agencies with regard to the processing, packaging, labeling and marketing of food products. Sources of information necessary for communication with government on public food policy information.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in FST 1250 , ABM 2010 , or NTR 1210 ; and C- or better in ENG 2105 or PHL 2020 .

courses.title: Food Safety and Current Issues
courses.description: [GE 5D] Overview of physical, chemical and microbiological hazards and their role in foodborne illness and the safety of the food supply. Introduction to the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point System. The role of government and basic aspects of food safety laws and regulations. Review of current issues in food safety, food protection, food production, and food processing as they relate to public health.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Meat Science
courses.description: Introduction to processing and utilization of fresh and value-added red meat products. Discussions on identity standards, factors affecting sensory, nutritional and shelf-life quality attributes, food safety (microbiological, chemical and physical hazards), including inspection and grading of red meats.

courses.title: Biotechnology Applications in Animal Science
courses.description: A study of the principles and practical applications of biotechnology in Animal Science. Discussion of the implications of genetic engineering, gene transfer, transgenic animals, embryo transfer and embryo manipulation for livestock improvement; present and future importance to the agriculture industry; human and veterinary medicine, ethical issues, patent law and strategies for future problem-solving. Appreciation of biotechniques with relevance to the Animal Sciences. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): AVS 4430LW .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 3305 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
courses.description: Cellular processes and molecular interactions, including transport, chemical signaling, cell-cell adhesion, intercellular communication, support and movement, energy conversions, digestion, assembly of macro-molecules and organelles, gene control in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2400 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: General Epidemiology
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of disease occurrence in human populations. Emphasis will be on descriptive epidemiology, formulation of hypotheses, analytic epidemiology, prevention and controls and case studies with problem solving.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L ; and STA 120, STA 1300 , BIO 211L or BIO 2110L .

courses.title: Molecular Biology Techniques Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experience with major techniques currently used in the isolation and analysis of proteins and nucleic acids. Emphasis is placed on column chromatography, gel electrophoresis, reverse-transcriptase-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and centrifugation techniques.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4320 .

courses.title: Medical Microbiology
courses.description: The pathogenesis of bacterial and fungal infections with an emphasis on morphological, biochemical, and virulence factors associated with host susceptibility to infection, laboratory methods of diagnosis and available treatment and prevention options.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Medical Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study the pathogenesis of bacterial and fungal infections. Identification and growth of microorganisms, as well as scientific thinking, are emphasized in the laboratory exercises. Corequisite(s): BIO 4635 .
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Food Process Engineering
courses.description: Process engineering principles and related calculations are introduced for food processing applications, including unit conversion, thermodynamics, material and energy balance, basic fluid mechanics, steady-state and unsteady-state heat transfer, psychrometry, and refrigeration. Corequisite(s): FST 3321L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 1220 or CHM 123; CHM 1220L or CHM 123L; PHY 1210 or PHY 121; PHY 1210L or PHY 121L; MAT 1200 or MAT 120; and FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Food Process Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Process engineering principles and related calculations are introduced for food processing applications, including unit conversion, thermodynamics, material and energy balance, basic fluid mechanics, steady-state and unsteady-state heat transfer, psychrometry, and refrigeration. Corequisite(s): FST 3321 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 1220 or CHM 123; CHM 1220L or CHM 123L; PHY 1210 or PHY 121; PHY 1210L * or PHY 121L; MAT 1200 or MAT 120; and FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Unit Operations in Food Processing
courses.description: An in-depth understanding of food processing technologies, including traditional and emerging methods. Explore the principles, equipment, and applications of various processing techniques such as dehydration, microwave processing, high-pressure processing, spray drying, extrusion, sous vide, and membrane filtration.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 2010 , CHM 201, CHM 3150 , or CHM 316; CHM 2010L , CHM 250L, CHM 3150L , or CHM 317L; FST 3321 or FST 332; FST 3321L or FST 332L; BIO 2060 or MIC 201; and BIO 2060L or MIC 201L.

courses.title: Food Chemistry
courses.description: Chemical, physical and functional properties of major and minor food components. Major components include water, carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and minor components include pigments, enzymes, vitamins, minerals and food additives. Chemical changes occurring to food components during processing and storage of foods. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): FST 4261LW .
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, and C- or better in the following: FST 2250 / FST 2250A , CHM 2010 or CHM 3150 , and CHM 2010L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Principles of Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point and Other Food Safety Management Systems
courses.description: Basic principles and application of the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) system in food and beverage manufacturing. Regulatory aspects, pre-requisite programs, and preliminary steps for plan design and implementation are also covered. Other food safety management systems, including Preventive Controls for Human Food will also be introduced. Corequisite(s): FST 4300A .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: BIO 3640 , FST 3640 , or MIC 201; BIO 3640L or MIC 201L; FST 3220 or FST 322; FST 3250 or FST 325; and FST 4170 or FST 417.

courses.title: Principles of Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point & Other Food Safety Management Systems Activity
courses.description: Basic principles and application of the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) system in food and beverage manufacturing. Regulatory aspects, pre-requisite programs, and preliminary steps for plan design and implementation are also covered. Other food safety management systems, including Preventive Controls for Human Food will also be introduced. Corequisite(s): FST 4300 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: BIO 3640 , FST 3640 , or MIC 201; BIO 3640L or MIC 201L; FST 3220 or FST 322; FST 3250 or FST 325; and FST 4170 or FST 417.

courses.title: Pesticide Laws and Regulations
courses.description: Federal and California Laws and Regulations affecting individuals, corporations, and agencies providing for the public health, safety and welfare; and protecting the environment including our natural resources. Emphasis on hazardous materials, ground water protection, pesticides, and pest control laws and regulation. Pesticide safety included. Function and structure of pertinent federal, state and county agencies and their enforcement practices as they relate to agribusiness, public health and pest control operations, including case studies.

courses.title: Environmental Toxicology
courses.description: Survey and analyses of the effects of civilization on the environment. Emphasis will be placed on the effects of agriculture and other forms of commerce on food, water, air, soil, and human health.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and PLT 231L or PLT 2310L .
